Class NetworkParams.IPRoute

java.lang.Object
oshi.software.os.NetworkParams.IPRoute
Enclosing interface:
NetworkParams
@PublicApi @Immutable public static final class NetworkParams.IPRoute extends Object
A single entry in the operating system's routing table.

The address family of the entry is given by the length of getDestination(): four bytes for IPv4, sixteen for IPv6. A route whose destination cannot be interpreted is omitted from NetworkParams.getRoutes(), so that length is always 4 or 16.

Platform notes: getMetric() is only reported on Linux, Windows and OpenBSD; macOS, AIX, Solaris, FreeBSD, DragonFly BSD and NetBSD do not publish a route metric. getPrefixLength() is -1 on the rare route whose netmask the operating system does not publish. getInterfaceIndex() is -1 when the interface name cannot be resolved to an index.

  • Constructor Details

    • IPRoute

      public IPRoute(byte[] destination, int prefixLength, byte[] gateway, String interfaceName, int interfaceIndex, long metric, boolean isGateway, boolean isHost)
      Constructs a new IPRoute instance.
      Parameters:
      destination - the destination network address bytes, four for IPv4 or sixteen for IPv6
      prefixLength - the number of leading bits in the destination network mask, or -1 if not published
      gateway - the next hop address bytes, or an empty array for a directly attached route
      interfaceName - the name of the outgoing interface, or an empty string if not published
      interfaceIndex - the index of the outgoing interface, or -1 if not published
      metric - the route metric or priority, or -1 if not published
      isGateway - whether the route forwards through the gateway rather than being directly attached
      isHost - whether the route is to a single host rather than to a network

  • Method Details

    • getDestination

      public byte[] getDestination()
      Gets the destination network address. For IPv4 routes this is a 4-byte array, for IPv6 routes a 16-byte array, so the length identifies the address family. A default route has an all-zero destination and a getPrefixLength() of 0.
      Returns:
      The destination address, never empty.

    • getPrefixLength

      public int getPrefixLength()
      Gets the number of leading bits in the destination network mask, as in CIDR notation.
      Returns:
      The prefix length, from 0 to 32 for IPv4 or 0 to 128 for IPv6, or -1 if the operating system does not publish the mask for this route.

    • getGateway

      public byte[] getGateway()
      Gets the next hop address that traffic matching this route is forwarded to. Only gateway routes have one. For a directly attached route the operating system may report the outgoing interface's own address, its link-layer address, or a symbolic name, none of which is a next hop, so all of them are reported as empty.
      Returns:
      The gateway address, 4 bytes for IPv4 or 16 for IPv6, or an empty array when isGateway() is false.

    • getInterfaceName

      public String getInterfaceName()
      Gets the name of the interface traffic matching this route leaves by.
      Returns:
      The interface name, or an empty string if the operating system does not publish one.

    • getInterfaceIndex

      public int getInterfaceIndex()
      Gets the index of the interface traffic matching this route leaves by, matching NetworkIF.getIndex().
      Returns:
      The interface index, or -1 if it could not be determined.

    • getMetric

      public long getMetric()
      Gets the cost of this route, used to select between routes to the same destination. Lower is preferred.
      Returns:
      The metric, or -1 on the platforms which do not publish one: macOS, AIX, Solaris, FreeBSD, DragonFly BSD and NetBSD.

    • isGateway

      public boolean isGateway()
      Tests whether traffic matching this route is forwarded through getGateway() rather than delivered directly on the attached link.
      Returns:
      true for a gateway route.

    • isHost

      public boolean isHost()
      Tests whether this route is to a single host rather than to a network, that is, whether getPrefixLength() covers the whole address.
      Returns:
      true for a host route.
